questions.prompt: In asyncio, what is the role of `await`?
choices: It pauses execution of the current coroutine until the awaited awaitable completes, allowing other coroutines to run
It blocks the entire Python process until the awaited operation finishes
It spawns a new OS thread to run the awaited operation concurrently
It converts a synchronous function into an asynchronous one
questions.correct_answer: It pauses execution of the current coroutine until the awaited awaitable completes, allowing other coroutines to run
questions.explanation: `await` suspends the current coroutine cooperatively (not blocking the event loop), yielding control so other tasks can proceed — core to asyncio's concurrency model.

distractor_rationales.It blocks the entire Python process unti: That describes synchronous blocking (e.g., `time.sleep()`), not `await`, which is non-blocking within the event loop.
distractor_rationales.It spawns a new OS thread to run the awa: Threading is separate; `await` works within a single thread using cooperative multitasking.
distractor_rationales.It converts a synchronous function into: `await` can only be used on already-awaitable objects (coroutines, Tasks, etc.); it does not convert functions.

questions.prompt: What is the primary use case for `weakref.ref`?
choices: To create a reference that does not prevent garbage collection of the referent
To force immediate garbage collection of an object
To create an alias for a variable with guaranteed lifetime extension
To track all active references to an object in real time
questions.correct_answer: To create a reference that does not prevent garbage collection of the referent
questions.explanation: `weakref.ref` creates a weak reference: it allows access to the object while not contributing to its reference count, so the object can still be garbage-collected when no strong references remain.

distractor_rationales.To force immediate garbage collection of: Weak references do not trigger GC; they merely don’t inhibit it.
distractor_rationales.To create an alias for a variable with g: A weak reference does *not* extend lifetime — the object may vanish at any time.
distractor_rationales.To track all active references to an obj: Python provides no built-in mechanism to enumerate all references to an object.

questions.prompt:

funcs = []
for i in range(3):
    funcs.append(lambda: i)
for f in funcs:

choices: UnboundLocalError
questions.explanation: All lambdas close over the same variable `i`. By loop end, `i == 2`, so each lambda returns 2 — classic late binding behavior in closures.

distractor_rationales.0\\n1\\n2: This would require each lambda to capture `i`'s value at definition time, which Python doesn’t do by default.
distractor_rationales.0\\n0\\n0: That would imply `i` remained 0, but the loop increments it to 2.
distractor_rationales.UnboundLocalError: No assignment to `i` inside the lambda makes it a free variable bound to the loop scope — no error occurs.
